> Motion and button controlled pet with an OLED display, humidity and temperature sensor and motion sensor. It is controlled by an ESP32 C3 Supermini. This is a guide, by SharKing Studios from Half-Life. To differ from the original guide, I have made my own personal sprite creation to show on the OLED display.

## Design

### 2026-10-11: I started following the tutorial for the starbie, placing the ESP32, DHT11, MPU6050, pinheaders and switches.

**0.98h**

I started following the tutorial for the starbie, placing the ESP32, DHT11, MPU6050, pinheaders and switches.
I then placed all the power symbols like GND, +3V3, +5V. I then added the netlabels and wired everything up, finishing the schematics with some no connect flags. Then, i assigned all the footprints and added the components to the PCB editor. After that, I placed the layout for the 6 point start edges and the components in a way that will be easy to use in the future. I then finished it by routing everything, adding GND coper fills on both sides and making sure there were no errors.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/bcb2d36d-cccf-4211-b346-72890a51dff4/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-11: First I downloaded a bunch of images based on the project theme like the half - life logo and some shooting stars. Then converted and downloaded them as KiCad footprints. This took quite a lot of trie

**1.05h**

First I downloaded a bunch of images based on the project theme like the half - life logo and some shooting stars. Then converted and downloaded them as KiCad footprints. This took quite a lot of tries as they were either to big or too small for the board. Then I installed the Arduino IDE and sorted out some of the parts for the BOM while keeping the cost as low ass possible. I then installed all the required libraries in the IDE based off the project guide. Lastly I tweaked some of the the routing and connections in KiCad for the MCU.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/4eb62287-9ae6-45fa-9695-06b459493912/video.mp4)

**0.68h**

First I started by drawing my personal sprite in pixilart.com and exporting it. Then I ran it through a converter so that it would be in the matrix format needed to paste it into the Arduino IDE. I was also AFK for the last 10 minutes of the timelapse for reasons I cannot remember.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/7e7bfa93-7af8-4165-aace-41011f129e0b/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-11: First I tried to get a basic understanding of the existing code so that it would be somewhat easier to edit the code later. Then I tried changing the fullness to anger  instead as I thought it would b

**2.05h**

First I tried to get a basic understanding of the existing code so that it would be somewhat easier to edit the code later. Then I tried changing the fullness to anger  instead as I thought it would be more interesting but when I ran the code, it resulted in lots of errors so I reset all the changes I made and followed the guide, and in the trail, pasting in my sprite matrix, and modifying one of the four options in the screen. Then I started making the repo. I wrote a basic introduction to the project, added some images, wrote instructed and made the BOM while also finalizing the rest of the parts for the starbie. I then exported the gerbers and used them to get a quote for the PCB and finish the pricing. I then uploaded all the existing files, added some more lines to the readme and made another BOM in excel and uploaded it as a CSV file to the repository.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/2d222ef3-7eea-4153-8366-ac33ceeaf447/video.mp4)
